card.title: Unseen passages and note-making — read to answer

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Comprehension is evidence hunting: read the QUESTIONS first, then skim for structure, scan for answers, and lift exact supporting lines. Note-making compresses a passage into ≤30 words via flowcharts (boxes + arrows, noun phrases, no full sentences). The seven stories and five poems train the same muscle on theme, character and device — 'The wind whispered' is personification whether in Burns or an unseen passage.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: method: questions → skim (gist) → scan (locate) → answer (quote + rephrase)  ·  flowchart notes: ≤30 words · boxes = stages · arrows = sequence · noun phrases only  ·  notice answers: what + when + where + who + action

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Answers must stay inside the passage — outside knowledge scores zero even when true. Flowchart notes keep the passage's ORDER and drop examples, repetitions and opinions. Notice/passage questions want stated facts first, vocabulary-in-context second, inference only where asked.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 'Importance of Clean Water' in ≤30 words as a flowchart (NEB 2024, 5 marks): source → treatment → supply → use → conserve — each box a noun phrase. Sports-day notice questions: report to the east ground — location traps hide in capitalised nouns. Literary device spot ('wind whispered' = personification, NEB 2023) works identically on seen poems and unseen lines.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Flowchart drill: read the water passage once, underline the five process nouns, chain them source→treatment→storage→distribution→conservation with arrows, count words (drop articles first). Five boxes, ~20 words, full marks — compression, not summarising in sentences (NEB 2024, 5-mark pattern).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Skim-scan fails dense argumentative passages (read those fully). Flowcharts flatten cause-effect nuance — fine for notes, fatal for essays. Device-spotting without effect-commentary ('it creates…') earns half marks; NEB wants effect, not labels.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: From story work to skill: 'The Selfish Giant' teaches theme-extraction (selfishness→sharing→redemption arc); transfer the same three-beat arc mapping to any unseen narrative. For poems: speaker → image → device → effect — run Burns's rose ('O my Luve's like a red, red rose' = simile + hyperbole of love) and the template fits any of the five poems.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Always read questions BEFORE the passage — they index where to scan. Numbers, names and capitals are visual anchors. Flowchart: nouns only, arrows only, count to 30. Device answers: name + quoted line + one-line effect.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (5): flowchart notes on 'Importance of Clean Water' (≤30 words). NEB 2023 (2–3): unseen global-warming passage + sports-day notice questions. Seen-text analysis (Last Lesson moment, device ID) from the literature bank.
